baseline: Sets, natural numbers, elementary logic and finite arithmetic are primitive vocabulary. Recursion expands every other recorded prerequisite; formal set-theoretic encodings, ZFC axioms, and size foundations for large categories are not part of this pedagogical route.

nodes.title: Drinfeld center of a monoidal category
nodes.description: For a monoidal category C, its center Z(C) has objects (X,c), where c is a half-braiding on X, and morphisms f:X→X′ compatible with the half-braidings. Tensoring these pairs makes Z(C) braided; C itself need not be braided.

nodes.title: Braided monoidal category
nodes.description: A monoidal category with natural isomorphisms c(X,Y):X⊗Y→Y⊗X satisfying the two hexagon identities.

nodes.title: Half-braiding
nodes.description: For an object X of a monoidal category C, a natural family of isomorphisms c_Y:X⊗Y→Y⊗X, compatible with tensor products and the unit: c_{Y⊗Z}=(id_Y⊗c_Z)∘(c_Y⊗id_Z), with associators inserted.

nodes.title: Monoidal category
nodes.description: A category C with a tensor bifunctor C×C→C, a unit object, and natural associativity and unit isomorphisms satisfying the pentagon and triangle identities.

nodes.title: Bifunctor
nodes.description: A functor C×D→E from a product of two categories to another category.

nodes.title: Natural isomorphism
nodes.description: A natural transformation whose component at every object is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Isomorphism in a category
nodes.description: A morphism f:X→Y having an inverse g:Y→X, so gf=id_X and fg=id_Y.

nodes.title: Natural transformation
nodes.description: A family of maps between the values of two functors, commuting with every morphism in their source category.

nodes.title: Product of categories
nodes.description: C×D has pairs of objects and pairs of morphisms, with identities and composition defined componentwise.

nodes.title: Functor
nodes.description: A map of categories preserving objects, morphisms, identities and composition.

nodes.title: Category
nodes.description: Objects and morphisms with associative composition and identity morphisms.

nodes.title: Cartesian product of sets
nodes.description: A×B is the set of ordered pairs (a,b) with a∈A and b∈B.

nodes.title: Composition of functions
nodes.description: For f:A→B and g:B→C, the composite g∘f:A→C sends x to g(f(x)).

nodes.title: Function between sets
nodes.description: An assignment taking each element of a specified domain set to exactly one element of a specified codomain set.

nodes.title: Ordered pair
nodes.description: A pair (x,y) with distinguished first and second entries; (x,y)=(x′,y′) exactly when x=x′ and y=y′.

nodes.title: Set
nodes.description: A collection of distinct elements, regarded as one object.

nodes.title: Chebyshev's inequality
nodes.description: If EX²<∞ and t>0, then P(abs(X−EX)≥t)≤Var(X)/t².

nodes.title: Markov’s inequality for nonnegative random variables
nodes.description: If Y is a nonnegative integrable real random variable and t>0, then P(Y≥t)≤E[Y]/t.

nodes.title: Variance of a real random variable
nodes.description: If EX²<∞, then Var(X)=E[(X−EX)²].

nodes.title: Expectation of an integrable real random variable
nodes.description: If E abs(X)=∫abs(X)dP<∞, the expectation of X is EX=∫X dP.

nodes.title: Linearity of the Lebesgue integral
nodes.description: If f and g are integrable real functions and a,b are real scalars, then af+bg is integrable and ∫(af+bg)dμ=a∫f dμ+b∫g dμ.

nodes.title: Monotonicity of the Lebesgue integral
nodes.description: If 0≤f≤g are measurable functions on a measure space, then ∫f dμ≤∫g dμ, allowing infinite integrals.

nodes.title: Lebesgue integral
nodes.description: For measurable f≥0, ∫f dμ is the supremum of integrals of nonnegative simple functions below f. For signed f with ∫abs(f)dμ<∞, define ∫f=∫f⁺−∫f⁻.

nodes.title: Real-valued random variable
nodes.description: A real-valued random variable is a measurable map from a probability space to ℝ with its Borel σ-algebra.

nodes.title: Measurable simple real function
nodes.description: A measurable real function with finite range. It can be written as a finite sum ∑ a_i 1_{A_i} with measurable level sets A_i.

nodes.title: Probability space
nodes.description: A probability space is (Ω,𝔽,P), where 𝔽 is a σ-algebra on Ω and P is a measure on 𝔽 with P(Ω)=1.

nodes.title: Borel σ-algebra on the real line
nodes.description: The σ-algebra on ℝ generated by the open intervals.

nodes.title: Finite set
nodes.description: A set X is finite if it is bijective with {1,…,n} for some integer n≥0; its cardinality is n.

nodes.title: Indicator function of a subset
nodes.description: For A⊆Ω, the real function 1_A is 1 on A and 0 on its complement.

nodes.title: Measurable map between measurable spaces
nodes.description: A function for which the preimage of each measurable subset of the codomain is measurable in the domain.

nodes.title: Measure
nodes.description: A measure μ maps a σ-algebra to [0,∞], sends ∅ to 0, and satisfies μ(⋃ₙAₙ)=∑ₙμ(Aₙ) for every pairwise disjoint sequence of measurable sets.

nodes.title: Bijection between sets
nodes.description: A function for which each element of the codomain is the image of exactly one element of the domain.

nodes.title: Disjoint sets
nodes.description: Two sets are disjoint when they have no common element; a family is pairwise disjoint when every two distinct members are disjoint.

nodes.title: Measurable space
nodes.description: A set equipped with a specified σ-algebra of subsets.

nodes.title: Open interval in the real line
nodes.description: For real a<b, the set (a,b)={x∈ℝ:a<x<b}.

nodes.title: Preimage of a subset under a function
nodes.description: For f:A→B and E⊆B, f⁻¹(E)={x∈A:f(x)∈E}.

nodes.title: Sum of a nonnegative series
nodes.description: For aₙ≥0, define ∑ₙ≥1aₙ as the supremum of its finite partial sums; the value may be infinite.

nodes.title: σ-algebra generated by a family of subsets
nodes.description: The smallest σ-algebra containing that family, equivalently the intersection of all σ-algebras on the ambient set that contain it.

nodes.title: Extended nonnegative real numbers
nodes.description: The nonnegative real numbers together with a greatest element ∞. Sums involving ∞ equal ∞, and 0·∞ is taken to be 0 when integrating simple functions.

nodes.title: Intersection of a family of sets
nodes.description: Inside a specified ambient set, the elements belonging to every member of the family.

nodes.title: Real sequence
nodes.description: A real sequence is a function a:ℕ₊→ℝ, written (aₙ)ₙ≥1.

nodes.title: σ-algebra
nodes.description: A σ-algebra on Ω contains Ω and is closed under complements in Ω and countable unions.

nodes.title: Complement of a subset
nodes.description: For A⊆Ω, its complement Ω∖A consists of the elements of Ω that do not belong to A.

nodes.title: Real number
nodes.description: A real number is an element of a complete ordered field ℝ; completeness means every nonempty subset bounded above has a least upper bound.

nodes.title: Sequence in a set
nodes.description: A function from the natural numbers, or the positive natural numbers, to that set.

nodes.title: Union of a family of sets
nodes.description: The set of elements belonging to at least one member of the family.

nodes.title: Least upper bound in a partially ordered set
nodes.description: For A⊆P, its least upper bound is an upper bound s satisfying s≤b for every upper bound b of A, when such an s exists.

nodes.title: Natural number
nodes.description: One of 0, 1, 2, …; natural numbers count finite collections.

nodes.title: Ordered field
nodes.description: A field with a total order preserved by addition, in which the product of two positive elements is positive.

nodes.title: Field
nodes.description: A commutative ring in which 1≠0 and every nonzero element is invertible.

nodes.title: Total order
nodes.description: A partial order in which any two elements are comparable.

nodes.title: Commutative ring with identity
nodes.description: An abelian group under addition, together with an associative commutative multiplication with identity, distributing over addition. The zero ring is allowed.

nodes.title: Partial order
nodes.description: A reflexive, antisymmetric and transitive binary relation, usually written ≤.

nodes.title: Abelian group
nodes.description: A group whose operation is commutative.

nodes.title: Binary relation on a set
nodes.description: A subset R⊆S×S; writing xRy means (x,y)∈R.

nodes.title: Group
nodes.description: A set with an associative binary operation, an identity element, and a two-sided inverse for each element.

nodes.title: Subset
nodes.description: A⊆B means every element of A is an element of B.

nodes.title: Binary operation on a set
nodes.description: A function S×S→S.

nodes.title: Cartesian product of sets
nodes.description: A×B is the set of ordered pairs (a,b) with a∈A and b∈B.

nodes.title: Function between sets
nodes.description: An assignment taking each element of a specified domain set to exactly one element of a specified codomain set.

nodes.title: Ordered pair
nodes.description: A pair (x,y) with distinguished first and second entries; (x,y)=(x′,y′) exactly when x=x′ and y=y′.

nodes.title: Set
nodes.description: A collection of distinct elements, regarded as one object.

variance requires linearity-lebesgue-integral in the selected definition or proof. Finite second moment implies integrability using |x|≤1+x²; no Hölder or Cauchy–Schwarz prerequisite is needed for this route.
markov-inequality requires expectation in the selected definition or proof. Integrate t·1_{Y≥t}≤Y. The integral of the indicator multiple is part of the simple-function integral formula.

chebyshev-inequality requires markov-inequality in the selected definition or proof. Apply Markov to (X−EX)². Its measurability follows by expressing level events as unions of preimages of real intervals; the elementary calculation stays in this note.
